**2026-02-02 10:05** – v3.2.1 – Hotfix (patch)
Deployed hotfix commit `b77e3d0` on top of v3.2.1. Fixes a timeout issue in the disbursement
status polling service. The service was holding connections open longer than the gateway
timeout, causing sporadic 504s for a small subset of grantee requests. Patch limits the poll
interval and adds a connection reuse flag. Post-deploy checks show error rate back to baseline.
– Author: Marcus T.

**2026-02-02 16:30** – Configuration change – Payment gateway integration
Added the new sandbox credentials for the payment gateway integration to the staging
configuration store. These credentials are for testing only and are not active in production.
Refer to the planned maintenance window on 2026-02-12 for the production gateway cutover.
Change reference: CFG-2026-0151.
– Author: Priya N.

**2026-02-03 09:00** – v3.2.1 – No release
No deployment today. Monitoring stable. Overnight batch job for grant eligibility checks
completed within SLA. No action required.
– Author: Aisha R.

**2026-02-03 13:20** – Configuration change – Feature flag
Enabled the feature flag `new_application_review_layout` for internal testers only (user group
`gnf-internal`). Flag is set to 10% rollout for the general applicant pool, but remains disabled
for all external users. Rollout plan documented in the change request CR-2026-0088.
– Author: Aisha R.

**2026-02-04 11:45** – v3.2.1 – Hotfix (patch)
Deployed hotfix commit `c99f1a4` to production. Addresses a data validation bug in the grant
application form where certain Singapore postal codes were rejected if they contained a leading
zero. The validation regex has been corrected. The deployment log records that the Grant
Management System version is v3.2.1. This hotfix does not change the version number; it is a

documents.content:
# GMS Monitoring Dashboard

## Configuration Overview

**System:** GNF Monitoring Dashboard (internal system health)
**Data source:** Operational telemetry from GMS Grant Management System and supporting infrastructure
**Retention:** 90 days raw metrics; 13 months 1-minute rollups
**Timezone:** All timestamps in SGT (UTC+8)

### Alert Configuration (current)

| Setting | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| alert_configured | true | Current |
| Notification channel | SMS (primary), email (secondary) | Current |
| SMS gateway | Singtel API, rate limit 20 msg/min | Current |
| Escalation policy | Page on-call after 2 consecutive 5-min windows above threshold | Current |
| Maintenance window | Daily 02:00–03:00 SGT | Current |
| Auto-resolution | Enabled, 15-min sustained below threshold | Current |

The monitoring configuration sets the GNF Monitoring Dashboard alert_configured to true. Record status: current. This setting has been in effect since 2025-11-03 and has not been modified during the incident window.

### Active Alert Rules

| Rule ID | Metric | Threshold | Severity | Window | Enabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-101 | cpu_usage | > 90% | CRITICAL | 5 min | Yes |
| R-102 | error_rate | > 3% | WARNING | 5 min | Yes |
| R-103 | p95_latency | > 500 ms | WARNING | 5 min | Yes |
| R-104 | memory_usage | > 90% | WARNING | 5 min | Yes |
| R-105 | db_connection_pool_exhaustion | pool at 100% | CRITICAL | 1 min | Yes |
| R-106 | queue_depth | > 50 | WARNING | 5 min | Yes |
| R-107 | payment_gateway_latency | > 800 ms | CRITICAL | 5 min | Yes |
| R-108 | payment_gateway_error_rate | > 2% | CRITICAL | 5 min | Yes |

**Note:** Rule R-107 (payment_gateway_latency) was added on 2026-02-12 at 14:30 SGT by Aisha Rahman (DevOps Lead) following the earlier payment gateway slowdown observed on 2026-02-11. Rule R-108 (payment_gateway_error_rate) was added at the same time. Both rules are currently enabled.

---

## Incident Timeline — 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-12 SGT

### 2026-02-10

**09:15** — Dashboard operational. No alerts active. All metrics within normal range.

**14:30** — Routine check. CPU 42%, memory 58%, error rate 0.2%, p95 latency 180 ms.

**18:00** — End-of-day summary: No alerts triggered. System stable.

---

### 2026-02-11

**08:45** — Pre-workload check. CPU 38%, memory 55%, error rate 0.1%, p95 latency 170 ms.

**10:20** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-103 (p95_latency > 500 ms). Current p95 latency: 540 ms. HTTP request rate: 410 req/min. CPU 62%, memory 61%. Error rate 0.3%. Duration: 1 window.

**10:25** — **ALERT CLEARED** — R-103. p95 latency: 480 ms. No further action taken.

**11:05** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-103 (p95_latency > 500 ms). Current p95 latency: 560 ms. HTTP request rate: 425 req/min. CPU 65%, memory 62%. Error rate 0.4%.

**11:10** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-103 (second consecutive window). Escalation page sent to on-call engineer (Marcus Tan). SMS sent.

**11:15** — **ALERT CLEARED** — R-103. p95 latency: 470 ms. Marcus acknowledged page at 11:14, noted investigation in progress.

**11:20** — Marcus logged into dashboard. Investigation notes: "Latency spikes coincide with batch job schedule. Checking if the batch job is causing contention with the API tier."

**11:35** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-101 (cpu_usage > 90%). Current CPU: 91%. p95 latency: 510 ms. Error rate: 0.5%. HTTP request rate: 430 req/min.

**11:40** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-101 (second consecutive window). Escalation page sent.

**11:45** — CPU: 93%. p95 latency: 550 ms. Error rate: 0.6%. Marcus notes: "Batch job appears to be consuming significant CPU. Checking job scheduler logs."

**11:50** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-101 (third consecutive window). Critical severity. Page sent to DevOps Lead (Aisha Rahman).

**11:55** — CPU: 94%. p95 latency: 580 ms. Error rate: 0.7%. Aisha joins investigation.

**12:00** — **ALERT TRIGGERED** — R-102 (error_rate > 3%). Current error rate: 3.2%. CPU: 95%. p95 latency: 620 ms. HTTP request rate: 435 req/min.
